title: API Compatibility & Deprecation Policy for Inference Services
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference's official API compatibility guarantees and the deprecation lifecycle for public inference endpoints and first-party SDKs (redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-js) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to give engineering and product teams a predictable, auditable process for evolving APIs while minimizing customer disruption.

Scope:

- Applies to all stable public HTTP/REST and streaming endpoints under the hostnames and service names: redwood-inference-api, dedicated-gateway, private-control-plane.
- Applies to first-party SDKs we publish (Python, JS, Go) and the official CLI.
- Does NOT apply to internal admin-only endpoints, experimental preview endpoints (labelled preview or beta), or off-the-record telemetry endpoints.

Key Principles:

1) Backwards compatibility is the default: we commit to non-breaking changes for stable endpoints unless explicitly communicated.
2) Predictability for customers: deprecation windows are fixed and conservative, with extra time for Private/on-prem deployments.
3) Observability-driven: every change must have telemetry and regression checks before, during, and after rollout.
4) Clear migration paths: provide code examples, SDK helper functions, and automated shim layers where feasible.

Compatibility guarantees (service-level):

- Patch (non-functional fixes, docs): no deprecation required.
- Minor (adds new optional fields, new query params that are ignored if absent): immediate live changes allowed; must be documented.
- Major (breaking semantics change: request/response schema changes, removed fields, removed endpoints, changed error semantics): requires deprecation procedure (see below).

Semantic versioning guidance (applies to API surface and SDKs):

- We adopt SemVer for SDK releases. Major version bumps indicate potential breaking changes.
- For HTTP APIs we expose an explicit versioning header: X-Redwood-API-Version (format: YYYY-MM-DD or v{major}).
- Stable endpoints will keep a canonical (unversioned) path backed by the latest compatible minor version; major changes must be exposed by a new versioned path or controlled via a header.

Deprecation lifecycle (standard timeline):

The following timeline is the default for Hosted (redwood-inference-api) and can be shortened only with approval. For Dedicated: same timeline unless customer contract specifies otherwise. For Private/on-prem: multiply windows by 2x (longer) to account for upgrade cycles.

- Announcement window: 90 days before sunset.
- SDK deprecation note: align with announcement; SDKs publish a deprecation PR with migration helpers the same day as announcement.
- Sunset/Removal: 90 days after announcement (i.e., endpoint removed after 90d).

Private deployment window (recommended): Announcement 180 days, removal 180 days.

Emergency breaking changes: changes required to mitigate security or severe reliability issues may be fast-tracked; these require sign-off from Security, SRE, and Product and a minimum 7-day notice with mitigation guidance.

Communication and notice contents:

Every deprecation announcement must include:
- Scope: exact endpoint(s), method(s), path(s), SDK versions affected.
- Rationale: why change is necessary.
- Migration path: code examples, schema diffs, and a checklist.
- Timetable: announcement date, sunset date, exceptions.
- Rollback plan and contact path (support alias + escalation phone).

Rollback and compatibility shims:

Engineering must prefer non-invasive shims where feasible, for example: server-side translation layers that accept old payloads and emit new payloads internally. If a shim is provided it must:
- Live for the full deprecation window.
- Be instrumented with a metric: shim_usage_{endpoint} and shim_errors_{endpoint}.

Observability & SLOs for deprecation rollout:

- Telemetry requirements before announcement: baseline traffic split by API version, major SDK versions in use, 95th/99th percentile latency, error rate by client version.
- During rollout we track: migration_rate (percentage of in-flight requests using new schema), customer_errors (4xx/5xx by account), and opt_in_header_usage.
- SRE guardrails: if customer_errors for a deprecating cohort exceed 0.5% above baseline for 3 continuous 5-minute windows, pause rollout and revert to previous behavior.

API change approval checklist (must be completed and attached to PR):

1. Schema diff (old -> new) included and formatted.
2. Backwards compatibility analysis (explaining why change is breaking or not).
3. Migration examples (curl + SDK) included.
4. Telemetry dashboards and alerts created (link to dashboard).
5. Ownership (service owner, SDK owner, product lead) assigned.
6. Security review (if applicable) completed.
7. Docs and changelog entry drafted.

Procedures: step-by-step deprecation process

1) Proposal & ADR: author files a design note or ADR describing the change and alternatives. Tag owners and SRE for early feedback.
2) Implementation behind flag: implement new behavior behind a feature flag (feature-flag:api-v2) and test with internal traffic and canary customers.
3) Telemetry verification: confirm non-regression on latency and error budgets for 2 weeks of canary traffic.
4) Announce deprecation: create a deprecation notice in the docs portal and send customer emails (platform-comm team) at T=0.
5) Provide SDK migration helpers: publish a minor SDK release with deprecation warnings and migration helpers.
6) Monitor: run daily checks on shim usage and customer errors.
7) Sunset: after the window, remove the endpoint and update the changelog and API reference.

Migration examples (concrete):

- Curl: opt-in to new API version via header

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-API-Version: 2026-02-01' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b", "input":"Hello"}'

- Python SDK (example shim helper):

from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=TOKEN, api_version='2026-02-01')
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-7b', input='Hello')

SDKs must provide a clear deprecation warning at import/runtime when a deprecated method is used, pointing to a migration guide URL.

Compatibility matrix (examples):

| Change type | Risk level | Hosted timeline | Dedicated timeline | Private timeline | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Add optional response fields | Low | Immediate | Immediate | Immediate | Document in changelog |
| Add new optional query param | Low | Immediate | Immediate | Immediate | No breaking behavior |
| Remove response field | High | 90d | 90d | 180d | Requires shim or major version |
| Change error codes (2xx -> 4xx) | High | 90d | 90d | 180d | Requires customer opt-in before change |

(Above table is illustrative; attach machine-readable schema diffs in the PR.)

Decision log (short):

- Decision: require minimum 90-day deprecation window for hosted endpoints.
  - Rationale: balances velocity with operational predictability and gives customers time to migrate.
  - Alternatives considered: 30/60/180-day windows. 30d considered too short; 180d slows platform iteration.

Ownership & escalation:

- Service owner: eng-serving-runtime (rotation: paging list: service-owner@redwood.internal)
- API product owner: product-api (product lead: Arman Rao)
- SDK owner: eng-developer-experience (lead: Priya Singh)
- Escalation path: support -> platform-ops -> oncall-sre -> product lead.

Appendices:

A. Example deprecation announcement template (copyable):

Subject: [Action Required] Deprecation notice: POST /v1/generate (legacy schema)

Hello {customer},

We are deprecating the legacy "/v1/generate" schema on 2026-05-01. This change enables X and Y (performance and safety improvements). To continue uninterrupted, update your client to send the new payload: [link to migration guide].

Timeline:
- Announced: 2026-02-01
- Sunset: 2026-05-01

If you need more time, reply to support@redwood.com with your account ID to request an extension (subject to contract).

B. Useful CLI commands for verifying shim usage:

# List top 10 customers still hitting legacy schema in last 24h
redwood-cli telemetry query --metric shim_usage_generate --window 24h --top 10

# Force opt-in header for a test account
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'X-Test-Account: acct_123' -H 'X-Redwood-API-Version: 2026-02-01' -d '{"input":"test"}'

C. Audit / Compliance notes:

- All deprecation announcements and customer extension approvals must be logged in the compliance tracker with ticket ID (format: DEP-YYYY-NNN).
- Security-impacting changes require an additional 48-hour escalation and an entry in the change management system.

How to adopt this policy (for engine/service teams):

1. Add "api-deprecation-checklist.md" to your service repo under docs/.
2. Create dashboard clones from the template: /confluence/templates/api-deprecation-dashboard.
3. Notify eng-platform and eng-sre 30 days before announcement for capacity planning.

Related documents and references:

- API design guidelines (endpoint naming, error semantics) — /confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/api-design-guidelines-2024
- Runtime compatibility ADRs — /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/runtime-compatibility-adr-2024

Questions or feedback: please open a PR against this doc or ping the reviewers list (Arman Rao, Priya Singh, Lena Sørensen).

-- End of policy document --
